sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 29 (check 28) and Internal Quality Checks row 29 (annotation: multiple verifiers are combined in one flow and need not be retested separately)
.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/rules/projects/webdev-task-template (file list; template criteria layout compared by structure only)
evidence:
Scope reviewed: all 52 criteria pairwise by observable (3 gate, 40 functional summing to weight 56.5, 6 polish, 3 visual likert). Hash check: all 43 frozen task files match manifest.json; all 15 raw-evidence artifacts match raw-evidence-index.json. That evidence is scripted golden behaviour only (its own limitations: no configured judge run, no test.sh launch path, no visual ratings), so compatibility of the whole criterion set in one product is supported by the scripted golden but not by a full judge run.

No true duplicate, no full subsumption and no pair demanding incompatible products was found. Pairs examined and why they hold: (a) cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic vs cw_same_line_carets vs cw_multi_caret_delete (functional/judge.toml:101,119,110): different-line atomic undo, same-line offset tracking ('Undo behaviour is not judged here'), and delete at carets are distinct observables. (b) cw_replace_all_atomic vs cw_replace_self_containing_text vs cw_replace_current (155,164,146): distinct fixtures and distinct outcomes (atomic undo/redo-clear, no rescan, advance to following match). (c) cw_output_before_failure_kept (245) explicitly disclaims the end reason scored by cw_time_limit_recovery (281) and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (290). (d) cw_caret_kept_in_view (83) grades automatic scroll-follow; cw_long_line_editing (92) grades no wrapping and manual horizontal reach. (e) cw_js/html_semantic_coloring and cw_visual_editor_readability (visual/judge.toml:24 'not whether token categories are correct') are separated; the three likerts carve typography, arrangement and finish apart. (f) Timing legs are mutually consistent: 4 s delayed markers sit inside the 5 s budget, time-limit legs allow about 10 s, live library allows 10 s against the brief's about 5 s. (g) Isolation (308), dynamic-code refusal (317), inline handlers in cw_html_preview (218) and whole-file error lines (227) can coexist in one product (sandboxed preview with a no-eval policy that still allows inline script).

Shared-precondition overlaps, judged acceptable under REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 and :19 and SKILL.md:64 but recorded: (1) cw_stale_save_keeps_draft (344) restates refusal, visible feedback and fresh-read-shows-A as a failing control, which is most of cw_stale_save_refused (335); an app that accepts stale saves loses both (3.0 of 56.5). The policy names exactly this split as two outcomes and requires the control, and 335 additionally grades history and the single new revision. (2) cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state (371, 'If A's library never shows B's snippet, this criterion fails as well') depends on the outcome of cw_live_library_update (362); with cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft (380) a missing live channel costs 5.0 of 56.5. The control is required so a dead feature earns no credit. (3) Last-good restoration is a leg in four criteria: cw_last_good_recovery (272, after throw, with input and canvas state), cw_time_limit_recovery (281), cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (290) and cw_dynamic_code_refused (317). These are different triggers of behaviour.md:5, so different observables, but an app with correct Stop cancellation and correct time limits and no restore loses 7.0 of 56.5 (12.4 percent of functional) for one missing behaviour. (4) cw_save_reload_restart (326) repeats the storage-clear readback already hard-gated by cw_shared_saved_record (gates/constraints/judge.toml:32); the gate has zero weight, so no score is double counted, only judge work.

One inconsistency between two criteria on Undo granularity (risk): cw_undo_restores_caret (128) says 'Press Undo repeatedly until both markers are gone', which accepts the character-by-character undo that ui.md:9 explicitly allows, while cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state (371) says 'Undo, pressed once or twice depending on how the app groups typing, must then remove that character and the marker'. See counterexample. This is not an incompatible-product demand (a grouping app passes both), so the row is not failed on it, but it is a conforming alternative that can fail and belongs with the hidden-requirement rows for reconciliation.

Not measured: no configured LLM judge run exists, so whether the judge actually keeps the sibling verdicts apart (prompt.md:10 'Never carry a verdict across criteria') is unobserved.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that can fail: an app that undoes single-caret typing one character at a time (allowed by environment/instructions/ui.md:9). The judge types a four-character marker and one more character in cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state; five Undo presses are needed, but functional/judge.toml:371 allows only 'once or twice', so after two presses three marker characters remain and a strict judge fails a 2.0-weight criterion although Undo history was preserved. The same app passes cw_undo_restores_caret (128), which lets Undo be pressed repeatedly. Weak app for the shared legs: correct Stop cancellation and time limits but no last-good restore fails 272, 281, 290 and 317 together.
suggested_fix: In cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state replace 'pressed once or twice depending on how the app groups typing' with 'pressed repeatedly until that character and the marker are gone', matching cw_undo_restores_caret. Optional: in cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_dynamic_code_refused, either keep the restore leg and accept the shared exposure, or reduce it to 'the second marker is not shown in the preview' so restore is graded by cw_last_good_recovery and cw_time_limit_recovery only; any such change needs the coverage map rechecked.
